title: reference-bench safeguard workflow for eval gating and prompt ownership
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a clear, auditable workflow connecting curated reference benchmark snapshots ("anchor benches") and prompt collections to automated regression gates. Without a defined stewarding and signing process, changes to evaluation prompt collections or CI config can silently shift score baselines and either block safe rollouts or allow regressions to reach customers.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight stewardship and artifact model for reference benchmark snapshots, plus an automated gating policy that ties model/config changes to mandatory eval runs. The mechanism should: (1) provide immutable, versioned benchmark artifacts with provenance and signer metadata; (2) expose role-based approval and diffing in Console; (3) surface deterministic gating decisions in CI and rollout workflows; (4) produce clear human playbooks for approving, rejecting, and rolling back model changes when regressions are detected.

Scope: This PM ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan. Engineering tickets will implement the artifact store, signing integration (KMS), CI hooks, and Console UI. Design will produce the approval UX and diff view. The outcome should enable automatic blocking of canary/production rollouts when regression thresholds are exceeded, and a manual override path tied to an approval audit log.
acceptance_criteria: Create a reference bench artifact spec (metadata: id, version, created_by, signer_hash, provenance URL, metric baseline definitions)
Define steward role and ACLs: who can create, propose, approve, and retire reference benches
Implement an immutable artifact location (S3-like store) with signed manifests and hash verification
CI integration: on model or inference-config changes, run evaluation harness against the linked reference bench and produce a deterministic pass/fail outcome
Gate policy defined: default regression thresholds per metric and per model family; pass/fail output surfaces in PR and rollout UI
Console: read-only diff between bench versions, approval button for exceptions, and audit log entry for all approvals/overrides
Run a small pilot (internal runtime team) and demonstrate blocking behavior on at least two intentionally induced regressions
Playbooks for rollback, canary throttling, and customer communication documented in Confluence
tasks: PM: finalize artifact metadata spec and steward ACL model
Design: mock Console diff and approval flows; create microcopy for approval/audit entries
Eng: implement artifact store API + signer integration (KMS) and manifest verification
Eng: add CI hook that triggers eval harness and posts gating result to PR and rollout controller
Eng: define metric bundle (accuracy@k, factuality heuristics, safety regressors) and baseline computation
Eng: implement automatic snapshotting of evaluation outputs and link to artifact
PM/Comms: draft stakeholder playbook and runbook for alerting and rollback
QA: create regression tests to simulate false positives/negatives on gating thresholds
decisions: Use an append-only artifact store with signed manifests instead of mutable database records to make rollbacks auditable
Default steward role limited to "bench-curator" group; approvers required for production-facing benches
Initial gate uses relative delta thresholds (e.g., >3% drop in primary metric OR 2 sigma for secondary metrics) with an explicit override flow
Signatures are KMS-backed HMACs recorded in the manifest; UI will show signer id and timestamp

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilot): Implement artifact spec, signer integration, and local CI gating for runtime-team models. Run deliberate regression tests and iterate on thresholds. Phase 2 (team rollouts): Open bench creation to product teams with curator role; enable Console diff UI and approval flow. Phase 3 (global): Default gating on all production rollouts, publish playbook, add telemetry for false positives. Each phase gated by pilot success metrics and a cross-functional readiness review.
risks_and_mitigation: False positives causing blocked releases -> mitigation: establish canary-only gating and manual approver override with required justification
Overhead for stewards -> mitigation: lightweight UI for proposing benches and automating common metadata, plus suggested baseline metrics from previous evaluations
Key compromise risk for manifest signer -> mitigation: use KMS with rotation and restrict signer to CI/service accounts; log all signing operations
Metric scope mismatch (bench not reflective of real traffic) -> mitigation: require provenance tags and traffic-representativeness metadata; run nightly coverage checks
